title: extcap: restore debug logging as ws_info log
description:
Default build (without WS_DEBUG #def) causes ws_debug to be a no-op  
See dc7f0b88, !3297

Would you agree "info" log level is "higher" than "debug" log level?  And you think these logging messages deserve to be shown in production builds?  Is any of our automated testing expecting this log strings as confirmation of behavior?

Are you trying to make sure ws_debug isn't a no-op?  Because I think most of these are "debug" level statements that are too verbose even for production and I'm fine with them not showing up.  There are a few that I would upgrade to ws_warning or ws_error when failure happens (can't load interface or create pipe).

But sometimes this just comes down to developer opinion.

[WSDG: 3.8.1.2. Logging Levels](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html/#ChSrcLogging)  
> By default logging output is generated for logging level "message" and above.  
  
A note like this should be added to any of the man pages (and perhaps WSUG) where log level is mentioned.  
  
There doesn't seem to be a canonical definition for log levels in `g_log()` or `ws_log()`.  
For system operation, syslog has a pretty clear list:  
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syslog#Severity_level  
```
<snip>
| 6 | Informational | info  |  | Informational messages | Confirmation that the program is working as expected.                                |
|---|---------------|-------|--|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 7 | Debug         | debug |  | Debug-level messages   | Messages that contain information normally of use only when debugging a program.[10] |
```
  
`extcap` should not be a black box that requires the end user to recompile to diagnose what's happening inside.  
Until there are multiple levels of "debug" logs (compile debug vs runtime debug) this is all that's available. The "info" level logs don't appear unless the used explicitly asks for them.
